Depending on the context, Larkin Love can refer to two very different things:

1. The Adult Entertainment Performer and Entrepreneur

Most commonly, Larkin Love is the stage name of an American adult film actress, cam model, and entrepreneur. Born on October 31, 1985, she is highly recognized within that industry for creating alternative and fetish-themed content (such as cosplay and role-playing). She is also an entrepreneur, running her own independent content website and brand.

2. "Larkin, Love and Jazz" / "Larkin: Love Again" (Media related to Philip Larkin)

If you encountered the phrase in a literary context, it likely refers to biographical media about the famous 20th-century British poet Philip Larkin.

  • Because his personal letters and journals revealed a highly complex, often cynical, and secretive romantic life with multiple simultaneous partners (such as Monica Jones, Maeve Brennan, and Betty Mackereth), several documentaries and biopics have been made focusing on this aspect of his life.
  • Notable examples include the BBC film Larkin: Love Again and the documentary Philip Larkin: Life, Love and Jazz.

Philip Larkin (1922–1985) was one of the most prominent and acclaimed English poets of the post-WWII era. He is widely regarded as the leading figure of "The Movement," a group of 1950s English writers who rejected the grand, complex romanticism of modernists like T.S. Eliot in favor of clear, structured verse written in plain language.

The Day Job: The Librarian Poet

Larkin spent the majority of his adult life working as a university librarian. For thirty years, he ran the Brynmor Jones Library at the University of Hull. He notoriously preferred the quiet, structured monotony of his day job to the spotlight of the literary world.

  • In 1984, he was offered the position of Poet Laureate of the United Kingdom (the nation's official poet), but he turned it down, deeply uncomfortable with the public profile and the expectation to write poems for royal events.

Style and Themes

Larkin's poetry is famous for being unsettling, deeply melancholy, and darkly witty. He wrote extensively about the mundane realities of mid-century British life, urban decay, loneliness, aging, and the terrifying inevitability of death.

While he could be fiercely cynical, his technical mastery allowed him to turn ordinary disappointment into hauntingly beautiful verse. Some of his most celebrated collections include:

  • The Less Deceived (1955)
  • The Whitsun Weddings (1964)
  • High Windows (1974)

Famous Lines

You have likely run across his work without realizing it. His poem "This Be The Verse" contains one of the most frequently quoted openings in modern English literature:

"They fuck you up, your mum and dad.
They may not mean to, but they do.
They fill you with the faults they had
And add some extra, just for you."

Another of his masterpieces, "Aubade," is widely considered one of the most raw and powerful meditations on the fear of death ever written.

Posthumous Controversy

During his life, Larkin was viewed as a somewhat grumpy, reclusive, but deeply cherished British institution. However, when his chosen biographer Andrew Motion published Philip Larkin: A Writer's Life in 1993, alongside a collection of Larkin's private letters, public perception shifted.

The letters revealed a highly problematic private persona: he was intensely misogynistic, frequently racist, obsessed with pornography, and maintained highly secretive, overlapping romantic relationships with multiple women at once. Today, he remains a deeply polarizing figure—widely condemned for his personal views, yet undeniably revered for his immense contribution to English literature.
